Recent work supports combining sequence encoders with global transition evidence: [TGCL4SR (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28789) models temporal item-transition graphs; [DGLSR (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ipm.2025.104119) represents graph nodes with Gaussian means/covariances to capture uncertainty. These motivate graph residuals, but embedding uncertainty is different from uncertainty about a rarely observed directed edge. Earlier [Bayesian nearest-neighbor research](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s41060-022-00367-4) explicitly separates popularity from personal taste, providing a closer conceptual foundation for popularity correction.

Practical synthesis, rather than a verified recipe from those papers: estimate directed training counts c_ij with a Dirichlet prior centered on destination popularity q_j. Posterior mean p_ij=(c_ij+αq_j)/(n_i+α), n_i=Σ_j c_ij, shrinks sparse rows toward popularity; use log(p_ij/q_j) as an association residual. This adapts established [Dirichlet smoothing](https://timan.cs.illinois.edu/czhai/pub/sigir2001-smooth.pdf). Posterior variance p_ij(1−p_ij)/(n_i+α+1) quantifies uncertainty under the multinomial model; repeated transitions within users weaken its independence assumption. Track distinct-user edge support and consider user bootstrap uncertainty. Popularity normalization measures association, not causal debiasing.

For fusion, partition training users into folds; construct counts and popularity priors excluding each scored user’s entire fold. This applies [out-of-fold stacking](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v137/yan20a/yan20a.pdf) to prevent transition self-evidence without changing benchmark splits. First validate a fixed-weight SASRec-plus-residual blend, including zero residual weight, using common macro HR@10. Learn a support-aware gate only after reproducible gains, using out-of-fold features; otherwise a gate can exploit memorized edges.
